title: Routine Postnatal Care: Mother and Baby Checks

evidenceAudit.scope: Healthy mother and baby from birth to 6 to 8 weeks in a Saudi primary health care centre or hospital postnatal service: the two timed postpartum visits, physical and mental health checks for the mother, the full examination of the baby within 72 hours, vitamin K and hepatitis B vaccine for the baby, anti-D for rhesus D-negative mothers, pain relief, infant feeding support, contraception, warning signs and referral. Uses the Saudi Ministry of Health Postpartum Visits page with NICE NG194 and the product labels.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-20.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: The Saudi Ministry of Health Postpartum Visits page gives only two visits (the first in the first week, the second at 4 to 6 weeks after birth); it does not list the detailed checks for the baby, so the baby checks follow NICE NG194, a United Kingdom guideline.

The Saudi national newborn immunisation schedule, the newborn metabolic and hearing screening programme and the Saudi vitamin K policy could not be opened; the Ministry childhood vaccination page says only that a first dose may be given at birth with another after two months. Hepatitis B vaccine timing here follows the Engerix-B label (0, 1 and 6 months) and must be matched to the Saudi schedule card.

Vitamin K prophylaxis: the US label gives 0.5 mg to 1 mg within one hour of birth as a single dose and prefers the subcutaneous route; the route used in local practice (usually intramuscular, 1 mg) is set by hospital policy and NICE intrapartum care guideline NG235 was not re-read for this topic.

Postpartum rubella or measles-mumps-rubella vaccination for non-immune mothers, iron treatment of anaemia and oral vitamin K schedules are mentioned but no label was reviewed and no regimen is written.
Anti-D immunoglobulin: only the 300 microgram dose within 72 hours is written; larger doses after a big fetomaternal bleed follow the Rhophylac label and local haematology advice.
The US ibuprofen and acetaminophen labels are over-the-counter drug facts labels; breastfeeding information for them was not reviewed beyond the label, so check a lactation reference.
The postpartum Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale and the NICE jaundice guideline NG98 were not read; they are referred to by name only.
Figures were read by automated extraction of web and label text; spot-check each dose against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: The womb shrinks and the lining sheds over several weeks (lochia); bleeding that becomes sudden, heavy or smelly suggests retained tissue or infection (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.13). Pregnancy and birth raise the risk of clots for about 6 weeks, so leg swelling, chest pain and breathlessness need urgent assessment (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.4). High blood pressure and pre-eclampsia can first appear or worsen after birth, often presenting as persistent or severe headache (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.4). The newborn has low stores of vitamin K and so can bleed in the first weeks; one dose at birth prevents this (Phytonadione label, Section 1.2). Mood changes, sleep loss and birth trauma affect many mothers, so wellbeing is checked at every contact (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.2). Young babies become seriously ill quickly and show non-specific signs such as poor feeding, abnormal colour, high or low temperature and fast breathing (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.4.9).

symptoms: Vaginal bleeding that slowly reduces over several weeks, with lower abdominal cramps (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.13).
Perineal or caesarean wound pain, breast fullness and tiredness (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.3).
Low mood, anxiety, poor sleep or distress about the birth (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.2 and Recommendation 1.2.5).
Problems passing urine or stool (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.3).
In the baby: feeding difficulty, no meconium within 24 hours, yellow skin, or a sleepy or unsettled baby (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.2 and Recommendation 1.4.9).
physicalSigns: Maternal blood pressure, pulse, temperature, uterine tenderness, wound and perineal healing, leg swelling and breast redness (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.3).
Baby appearance, colour, breathing, tone, hips, heart, red reflex and cord condition at the full examination within 72 hours (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.3).
Baby weight and head circumference plotted on a growth chart in the first week and at around 8 weeks (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.6).
At 6 to 8 weeks the baby shows social smiling and fixes and follows with the eyes (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.5).
redFlags: Sudden or very heavy vaginal bleeding, clots or tissue passed: assess as secondary postpartum haemorrhage and refer urgently (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.4 and Recommendation 1.2.14).
Fever, shivering, abdominal or perineal pain or foul-smelling discharge: suspect infection or sepsis and refer the same day (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.4 and Recommendation 1.2.8).
Leg swelling and tenderness, shortness of breath or chest pain: suspected venous thromboembolism; refer as an emergency (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.4).
Persistent or severe headache: check blood pressure and exclude pre-eclampsia (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.4).
Thoughts of self-harm or harming the baby, or signs of psychosis: urgent mental health assessment (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.2).

Baby red flags: ill appearance, pale, mottled or blue colour, unrousable, weak or high-pitched cry, grunting, breathing faster than 60 breaths a minute, chest indrawing, temperature 38 degrees Celsius or higher or below 36 degrees Celsius, non-blanching rash, bulging fontanelle, seizures, projectile or green vomiting: immediate emergency assessment (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.4.9 and Recommendation 1.4.10).
Baby has not passed meconium within 24 hours: needs medical advice (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.2).
precipitants: Caesarean birth, perineal tear or instrumental delivery raise wound and infection risk (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.3).
Anaemia and low weight before pregnancy worsen the effect of secondary postpartum bleeding (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.14).
Diabetes, hypertension or pre-eclampsia in pregnancy need blood pressure and glucose checks after birth (Saudi MOH Postpartum Visits page, Section Importance of postpartum visits).
Past mental health problems, traumatic birth or lack of support raise the risk of postnatal depression (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.5).
Late preterm birth, feeding problems or a mother with hepatitis B raise the baby's risk (Engerix-B label, Section 2.1).

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Heavy or increasing bleeding with clots or tissue, pain, fever or foul discharge (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.4 and Recommendation 1.2.13).
Unilateral leg swelling and tenderness, breathlessness or chest pain (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.4).
Severe or persistent headache with raised blood pressure (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.3 and Recommendation 1.2.4).
Red, swollen, tender breast persisting more than 24 hours despite self-management (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.4).
Persistent low mood, loss of interest, anxiety or intrusive thoughts at any contact (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.2).

differentials.condition: Serious illness in the baby (infection, sepsis, heart or bowel disease)
differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Any red flag in Recommendation 1.4.9: colour change, breathing, temperature, cry, vomiting or seizures (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.4.9).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: 140/90 mmHg or higher, or a rise with headache
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Measure at the first visit and for any mother who had a problem in pregnancy or after birth (Saudi MOH Postpartum Visits page, Section Importance of postpartum visits; NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.3).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Pallor, tachycardia or fatigue with a low haemoglobin
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Check when there is heavy bleeding, symptoms of anaemia or risk factors (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.3 and Recommendation 1.2.14).
ruleIn.normalValue: Haemoglobin within the adult female reference range of the reporting laboratory

ruleIn.testName: Full physical examination of the baby (newborn and infant physical examination)
ruleIn.targetCondition: Heart, hip, eye, genital or other congenital problem
ruleIn.expectedFinding: Murmur, absent red reflex, hip instability, undescended testes or other abnormality
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Done within 72 hours of birth and at 6 to 8 weeks; refer any abnormality (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.3).

ruleIn.expectedFinding: Visible jaundice in the first 24 hours or bilirubin above the treatment line
ruleIn.clinicalRationale: Assess yellow colour at each contact and follow the NICE jaundice guideline for measurement and treatment thresholds (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.7).
ruleIn.normalValue: No visible jaundice or bilirubin below the treatment threshold for age

ruleOut.modalityTarget: Screen for inherited metabolic and other disease
ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Carry out in line with the national newborn screening programme (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.9).

ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Carry out in line with the national hearing screening programme (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.10).

ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Give anti-D within 72 hours only if the baby is rhesus D positive or unknown (Rhophylac label, Section 2.2).

ruleOut.clinicalRationale: Ask about mood and anxiety at every contact and refer for assessment if there are concerns (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.2).

clinicalManagement.title: First postpartum visit
actions: Book the first visit in a primary health care centre in the first week after birth (Saudi MOH Postpartum Visits page, Section Postpartum visits).
Check the mother's health, mood, bleeding, pain, wound or perineum, breasts, bladder and bowels, and legs (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.3).
Check blood pressure and glucose when there was a problem in pregnancy or after birth (Saudi MOH Postpartum Visits page, Section Importance of postpartum visits).
Give the warning signs that need urgent care and ask about her birth experience (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.4 and Recommendation 1.2.5).

clinicalManagement.title: Examine the baby fully
actions: Examine appearance, head, eyes including red reflex, mouth, heart, lungs, abdomen and cord, genitalia, spine, skin, tone and hips (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.3).
Ask about feeding, passing urine and meconium within 24 hours, and weigh the baby (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.1, Recommendation 1.3.2 and Recommendation 1.3.6).
Check yellow skin colour and arrange bilirubin testing if jaundiced (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.7).
Arrange newborn blood spot and hearing screening (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.9 and Recommendation 1.3.10).

clinicalManagement.title: Give the medicines and vaccines
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At birth and the first days
actions: Offer vitamin K to the baby as a single dose within one hour of birth after explaining it to the parents (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.4; Phytonadione label, Section 2.3).

Give hepatitis B vaccine to the baby as the local schedule directs; if the mother is hepatitis B surface antigen positive give vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin within 12 hours (Engerix-B label, Section 2.1).
If the mother is rhesus D negative and the baby is rhesus D positive or unknown, give anti-D within 72 hours (Rhophylac label, Section 2.2).
Offer ibuprofen or paracetamol for pain, and discuss vaccines the mother needs (Saudi MOH Postpartum Visits page, Section Importance of postpartum visits).

clinicalManagement.title: Support feeding and bonding
actions: Ask about breastfeeding, positioning, latch, nipple pain and breast symptoms, and support continued breastfeeding (Saudi MOH Postpartum Visits page, Section Importance of postpartum visits; NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.11).
Discuss safe sleeping, cord care, skin care, crying and parent-baby attachment (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.11).

clinicalManagement.title: Second postpartum visit
actions: Review the mother's recovery, bleeding, mood and wound or perineum, and check blood pressure and sugar if there was a problem (Saudi MOH Postpartum Visits page, Section Postpartum visits and Section Importance of postpartum visits).
Discuss family planning and start a method, including the contraceptive topic in the Family Planning guideline (Saudi MOH Postpartum Visits page, Section Importance of postpartum visits).
Ask about vaginal discharge, sex, pelvic floor exercises and pain; refer to physiotherapy if needed (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.1 and Recommendation 1.2.7).

Examine the baby fully again, weigh and measure the head, check social smiling and following with the eyes, and check immunisation (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.3.3, Recommendation 1.3.5 and Recommendation 1.3.6).

clinicalManagement.title: Escalate concerns
actions: Refer the mother with heavy bleeding, sepsis signs, thromboembolism signs or severe headache to hospital the same day (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.4 and Recommendation 1.2.8).
Arrange immediate emergency assessment for any baby red flag (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.4.9 and Recommendation 1.4.10).
Refer low mood or anxiety for mental health assessment and ask about safety at home (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.2 and Recommendation 1.2.1).

regimens.indication: Prevention of vitamin K-deficiency bleeding in newborn babies
regimens.dose: 0.5 mg to 1 mg as a single dose within one hour of birth (Phytonadione label, Section 2.3). Dilution and preparation: for prophylaxis use the ampoule or syringe as supplied; if dilution is needed for treatment use only 0.9% sodium chloride, 5% dextrose or 5% dextrose in sodium chloride and give straight away; protect from light and discard the remainder (Phytonadione label, Section 2.4).
regimens.route: Subcutaneous injection whenever feasible; intravenous and intramuscular routes carry a boxed warning for severe hypersensitivity and are used only if the subcutaneous route is not feasible and the risk is justified; if intravenous, no faster than 1 mg per minute (Phytonadione label, Section 2.1 and Boxed Warning)
adjustments: Treatment of vitamin K-deficiency bleeding in a neonate is 1 mg subcutaneously or intramuscularly; use a higher dose if the mother took oral anticoagulants (Phytonadione label, Section 2.3).
Overdose in premature babies can cause haemolysis, jaundice and hyperbilirubinaemia (Phytonadione label, Section 8.4).
Local policy may set the route and dose; the route used in practice is a local decision (Phytonadione label, Section 2.1).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Observe for hypersensitivity: flushing, sweating, breathing difficulty, shock (Phytonadione label, Section 5.1).
Skin reactions at the site up to a year later (Phytonadione label, Section 5.2).
Jaundice and bleeding in the first weeks (Phytonadione label, Section 8.4).
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to phytonadione or any component of the medicine (Phytonadione label, Section 4).

regimens.indication: Prevention of hepatitis B infection in newborn babies
regimens.patientGroup: Babies of hepatitis B surface antigen-negative or positive mothers
regimens.dose: 0.5 mL (10 microgram) per dose at 0, 1 and 6 months; babies of mothers with hepatitis B surface antigen also receive hepatitis B immune globulin within 12 hours of birth (Engerix-B label, Section 2.1 and Table 1). Dilution and preparation: none; shake the vial or syringe well to a cloudy white suspension and inspect for particles; do not dilute.
regimens.route: Intramuscular injection into the anterolateral thigh in infants; do not use the buttock because the response is poorer (Engerix-B label, Section 2.2)
regimens.frequency: Dose 1 at birth or as the Saudi schedule directs, dose 2 at 1 month, dose 3 at 6 months; schedules with an extra dose at 2 months are also in the label (Engerix-B label, Section 2.1)
regimens.duration: Three-dose primary course; later boosters only if advised
adjustments: Subcutaneous use only in people at risk of bleeding with intramuscular injection; it gives a lower antibody response (Engerix-B label, Section 2.2).
Apnoea can follow intramuscular vaccination in babies born prematurely; decide timing from the baby's condition and the mother's hepatitis B status (Engerix-B label, Section 5.4).
Latex-containing syringe tip caps and yeast protein may matter for allergic babies (Engerix-B label, Section 11).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Observe for allergic reaction after the injection (Engerix-B label, Section 5.1).
Record the dose date on the immunisation card and book the next dose (Engerix-B label, Section 2.1).
Antibody testing after the course for babies of hepatitis B surface antigen-positive mothers (Engerix-B label, Section 2.6).
contraindications: Severe allergic reaction such as anaphylaxis after a previous dose of any hepatitis B vaccine or to a component, including yeast (Engerix-B label, Section 4).
regimens.sourceTitle: ENGERIX-B (hepatitis B vaccine, recombinant): US prescribing information (DailyMed)
regimens.sourceEdition: Engerix-B US label, Section 2.1, Section 2.2, Section 2.6, Section 4 and Section 5.4

regimens.indication: Prevention of rhesus D sensitisation after birth of a rhesus D-positive or unknown baby
regimens.dose: 300 microgram (1,500 IU) as a single dose within 72 hours of birth (Rhophylac label, Section 2.2); more if the fetomaternal bleed exceeds 15 mL of fetal red cells. 1 microgram equals 5 IU: do not confuse the units. Dilution and preparation: none; use the prefilled syringe as supplied, at room temperature, inspect for particles, do not freeze, single use.
regimens.route: Intramuscular or intravenous injection; if intramuscular and more than 5 mL, divide between sites; never subcutaneous; observe for at least 20 minutes (Rhophylac label, Section 2.1)
regimens.frequency: Once after birth, if the baby is rhesus D positive or unknown
adjustments: Do not give live virus vaccines within 3 months (Rhophylac label, Section 7.1).
Passive anti-D may show on later antibody screens (Rhophylac label, Section 5.2).
Not for the newborn (Rhophylac label, Section 4).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Observe for 20 minutes for hypersensitivity (Rhophylac label, Section 2.1).
Fetomaternal haemorrhage test to check the dose is enough (Rhophylac label, Section 2.2).
Record the batch and date on the maternal record (Rhophylac label, Section 2.1).
contraindications: Anaphylactic or severe systemic reaction to human immune globulin (Rhophylac label, Section 4).
IgA-deficient patients with antibodies to IgA and a history of hypersensitivity to the product (Rhophylac label, Section 4).
Mother not rhesus D negative, already sensitised, or baby rhesus D negative (Rhophylac label, Section 1.1).

regimens.patientGroup: Adult women after vaginal or caesarean birth
regimens.dose: 200 mg to 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours as needed, with no more than 1,200 mg in 24 hours unless a doctor directs (Ibuprofen label, Directions). Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet.
regimens.route: Oral with water; take with food or milk if the stomach is upset (Ibuprofen label, Directions)
regimens.duration: Shortest time possible; ask a doctor if pain lasts more than 10 days (Ibuprofen label, Stop use)
adjustments: Check the label and a lactation reference for breastfeeding; the over-the-counter label asks breastfeeding women to ask a health professional before use (Ibuprofen label, Pregnancy or breast-feeding).
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest time (Ibuprofen label, Directions).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Stomach pain, black stools or vomiting blood: stop and seek care (Ibuprofen label, Stop use).
Pain that increases or is severe at the perineum or wound: examine for infection or haematoma (NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.3).
contraindications: Previous allergic reaction to ibuprofen or other pain relievers, including aspirin-triggered asthma (Ibuprofen label, Do not use).
Right before or after heart surgery (Ibuprofen label, Do not use).
Ask a doctor first with stomach ulcer or bleeding, kidney disease, heart disease, high blood pressure, liver cirrhosis or a diuretic (Ibuprofen label, Ask a doctor before use).
regimens.useWhen: First choice for perineal, wound or uterine cramp pain when she has no stomach, kidney or aspirin-sensitive asthma problem.

regimens.sourceEdition: NICE NG194, Recommendation 1.2.3; Ibuprofen label, Section Directions

regimens.indication: Short-term pain relief after birth for women who cannot take an anti-inflammatory tablet
regimens.dose: 500 mg to 1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed; no more than 3,000 mg in 24 hours on the over-the-counter label (Acetaminophen label, Directions). Dilution and preparation: none; oral tablet.
regimens.duration: Shortest time possible; ask a doctor if pain lasts more than 10 days (Acetaminophen label, Stop use)
adjustments: Do not take with any other acetaminophen-containing product (Acetaminophen label, Do not use).
Warfarin users should ask a doctor or pharmacist (Acetaminophen label, Ask a doctor or pharmacist).
SFDA: the Saudi Food and Drug Authority register could not be opened from this environment, so registration of this product in Saudi Arabia was not verified; check the register before prescribing.
monitoring: Skin reaction: stop and seek care (Acetaminophen label, Allergy alert).
Liver injury risk with alcohol or overdose (Acetaminophen label, Liver warning).
contraindications: Allergy to acetaminophen or an inactive ingredient (Acetaminophen label, Do not use).
Liver disease: ask a doctor before use (Acetaminophen label, Ask a doctor before use).
regimens.useWhen: Choose when ibuprofen is not suitable.

teaching.scope: Healthy mother and baby from birth to 6 to 8 weeks in a Saudi primary health care centre or hospital postnatal service: the two timed postpartum visits, physical and mental health checks for the mother, the full examination of the baby within 72 hours, vitamin K and hepatitis B vaccine for the baby, anti-D for rhesus D-negative mothers, pain relief, infant feeding support, contraception, warning signs and referral. Uses the Saudi Ministry of Health Postpartum Visits page with NICE NG194 and the product labels.
learningObjectives: Offer two visits: in the first week and at 4 to 6 weeks.
Check the mother's bleeding, pain, mood, blood pressure and wound at each contact.
Examine the baby fully within 72 hours and again at 6 to 8 weeks.
Give vitamin K and hepatitis B vaccine, and anti-D when needed.
pitfalls: Skipping the baby examination within 72 hours.
Not checking blood pressure after a hypertensive pregnancy.
Forgetting anti-D for a rhesus D-negative mother.
keyPoints: Teach the mother the warning signs of heavy bleeding, infection, clots and headache.
Any baby red flag needs immediate emergency assessment.
Do not forget the 6 to 8 week mother and baby review.
Ask about mood at every contact.

patientEducation: Bleeding after birth slowly gets lighter over a few weeks; go to hospital if it becomes sudden, heavy or smelly.
Come back for the first visit in the first week and the second at 4 to 6 weeks.
Go to hospital for fever, calf pain or swelling, chest pain, breathlessness or a severe headache.
Feed your baby on demand; ask for help with latch or sore nipples.
Take your baby's vaccination card to every visit.
Tell us if you feel low, anxious or cannot cope.
lifestyleAndDiet: Rest when the baby sleeps and accept help at home.
Eat balanced meals and drink enough water, especially while breastfeeding.
Walk gently and build up activity slowly.
Place the baby on the back to sleep and keep the room smoke-free.
mdtReferrals: Primary care physician; midwife or postnatal nurse; obstetrician and gynaecologist; paediatrician or neonatal nurse; lactation consultant; mental health professional; pharmacist; physiotherapist.
dischargeCriteria: Date of birth and mode of birth recorded; first visit booked in the first week; vitamin K and hepatitis B vaccine recorded on the baby's card; anti-D given if needed; feeding plan agreed; warning signs explained; contraception discussed.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: First visit in the first week; second visit at 4 to 6 weeks for mother and baby; doctor review at 6 to 8 weeks; further follow-up as needed for blood pressure, glucose, mood and baby growth.
